title: Continue is cheaper, but a design-heavy stage would cross the compaction point
brief: Today is {{TODAY}}. Harness: Claude Code CLI. The harness reports this session's model as claude-opus-5-5 at effort high.

/context reports 126,450 tokens in use of a 200,000-token window. This installation compacts automatically at 80 percent of the window (160,000 tokens), as its settings state. This session has not been compacted.
A fresh session in this harness and project starts at 86,450 tokens (measured last week with /context before any message).

Next stage: evaluation design for a ranking procedure: choose the test cases, define the measures and write the runner's brief. Plan estimate: 12 turns. On the previous design stage in this project, fresh input averaged 2,500 tokens per turn and output 1,500 per turn (measured).
A fresh session would read 30,000 tokens: the procedure, the handoff and the prior results.
A handoff for this stage would be about 80 lines. If an acceptance session were used, it would take about 15 turns and read about 40,000 tokens.
Everything this session knows that the next stage needs is already written in files on disk.
No cache-miss measurement exists, and no review pauses are expected during the stage.
The stage writes files and commits locally; nothing leaves the machine.
notes: C_end passes K, so a compaction is ahead; the compaction penalty is smaller than the fresh session's first read, so the arithmetic favours continue by more than 10 percent.
Guardrail 2 makes the final verdict fresh: the stage is design-heavy and would cross K.
